subject: dsa
title: Coin Change II
summary: dp[i][a] counts the distinct combinations of the first i coins that sum to amount a. Introducing a coin adds the combinations that reuse it: dp stays the row above plus dp at the same row, amount minus the coin.
problem: Count the distinct combinations of coins = [1, 2] that sum to amount = 4. Rows are coin sets (no coins, then +coin 1, then +coin 2); columns are amounts 0 through 4. dp[i][a] is the number of ways to make amount a.

steps.caption: Columns are amounts 0 through 4 and dp counts the ways to make each amount. With no coins there is one way to make 0 and no way to make the rest.
Add coin 1. Every amount is reachable exactly one way using only 1s, so the whole row becomes 1.
Add coin 2: dp[a] = the value above + dp at this row, amount minus 2. That gives 1, 1, 2, 2, 3 across the amounts.
The bottom-right cell is 3, so 3 combinations make 4: 1+1+1+1, 1+1+2, and 2+2.
